verdicts.evidence: Exact copy of expectedRules's guard, same post-condition of rulesDir: dir is either the mission's rules/ (existence checked by rulesDir), or the package's templates/rules (shipped through "files", checked) — the guard only fires on a mutilated node_modules, outside the input universe, a state runward doctor already condemns. Measured on every real input: zero difference (full battery, mission without rules/ on the fallback). Sensitivity control, corrupted state rebuilt (templates without rules/): shipped → ordered red exit 1 (41 violations); mutated → exit 1 too, audit replaced by "✗ ENOENT ... scandir .../templates/rules" — same exit code, divergence confined to a corrupted installation that the analysis presupposes intact.

verdicts.evidence: The tightest of the four guard mutants: reachable only on the same corrupted state (package without templates/rules AND mission without rules/), and EVEN THERE, measured byte for byte identical — the known universe goes from {} to {"Stryker was here"}, but the "unknown rule" check only changes for a manifest row literally named "Stryker was here", which does not exist; diff of shipped/mutated outputs on the rebuilt state: 0 lines, exit 1 on both sides. On every real input (intact package) the return is dead by the post-condition of rulesDir. Sensitivity control closed twice over: it would take a mutilated package AND a manifest citing the mutant's literal.

verdicts.evidence: Same mechanics as its twin in expectedRules but on the UNIVERSE of known slugs (the "unknown rule" check). RECIPE: the same cli-infix mission (rule a.mdx.md HIGH/architect, n/a row "a.mdx" in architecture.md, lock re-signed). MEASURED: shipped → known contains "a.mdx", the row is recognised, exit 0; mutated → known contains "ax.md", the legitimate row is rejected "✗ Architect · a.mdx — unknown rule (typo? not in runward/rules/)", exit 1 — the gate accuses the exact slug of the rule that is present of being a typo, a remediation impossible as stated (the unmutated expectedRules keeps requiring "a.mdx": the mission can no longer be green). Nothing sees it: no shipped name and no fixture of the net has an infix ".md".
